title: The wire: org types
description: Part of the source of every type on the wire (#1135, #5380): one file per domain in Packages/Wire/schema. A $ref to another file names it (core.schema.json#/definitions/JSONValue); scripts/wire.sh gen reads them all.

AccountKey.description: An outside account by what tells it from the others (#5253): its service and address, as the control plane matches them, case aside.

AccountLastOp.description: An account's newest operation (#4157), for the time ago its row shows.

agent.description: The session that did it: by manage_accounts, or by reading the secret or card the account names. Left out when no session did.

AccountOperation.description: One read or change of an outside account by manage_accounts (#4157): a get, a list filtered to its service, or an add. Never a value of the account but its service and address.

agent.description: The session whose manage_accounts call it was.

AccountOperationWhat.description: What an operation on an account was (#4157): read (by manage_accounts, or a read of its secret or card), added, edited (it took another's place), or removed (#5253). An account's lastOp is never removed: a removed account has none.

AccountProfile.description: An account added to a runtime (#840), beside the runtime's own sign-in, which is the Default account and is not one of these. The person picks one when they start a session.

id.description: The host's own name for it. An agent keeps it as accountID.

name.description: What the person called it, such as Work.

signedIn.description: Whether its folder holds a sign-in, as the host read it when it answered.

signedInAs.description: Who it is signed in as, such as an email address, when the runtime's files say.

signInCommand.description: The command that signs it in, in a terminal on the host, for a runtime the app cannot sign in itself (Claude). Absent for one that signs in with runtimes/authenticate.

source.description: Who gave the account (#999): absent or person for one the person added, organisation for an org route, which the person cannot remove.

isDefault.description: The runtime's default account for new sessions (Reaches the Model By, #999). When no account says so, the runtime's own sign-in is the default.

setBy.description: The organisation's policy refuses this account (#999, runtimes.<id>.reach).

AccountReach.description: How an account reaches the model (#840): a sign-in kept in a folder of its own, or (#999) an organisation's route: an org key or a gateway, through the machine's model relay.

folder.description: The folder the runtime is given in its account variable (Runtime.accountFolderVariable).

AuditActor.description: Who did something through the control plane (#996, spec 736 FR-039), as the control plane wrote it: never taken from a client. A person and their client, or a bot and the event that started it. On a control plane with one person, the user is always the local owner.

scim.description: A SCIM write: the user is scim:<provider> (#1002).

refresh.description: A suspension by a refused refresh: the user is the suspended person (#1002).

AuditCause.description: The event that started a bot's action (#996).

AuditDays.description: control/setAuditDays (#996): how many days audit entries are kept, 1 to 3,650. The default is 90.

AuditEntry.description: One audit entry (#996): who did what, on which machine, and when. `action` is in words; `method` is the call it came from.

AuditExport.description: audit/export's answer (#996): the entries as JSON lines, oldest first, at most 50,000.

AuditList.description: audit/list's answer (#996): entries newest first, how many days the control plane keeps them, and whether older ones were left out.

admin.description: Whether the caller sees every person's entries.

AuditQuery.description: audit/list and audit/export (#996): a time range and, for an admin, one person. A member sees only their own entries, whatever `user` says.

limit.description: At most this many, newest first; 200 when absent, never more than 1,000.

AuditRefresh.description: A suspension by a refused refresh (#1002, Q1 A): the provider that refused.

AuditSCIM.description: A SCIM write's actor (#1002, D16): the provider and the id of the token it used, never its value.

AuditSink.description: One audit sink (#1001). `address` is tcp://host:port or tls://host:port for syslog, an https:// URL for HTTP. `token`, for HTTP, is sent as a bearer token; it is only ever sent to the control plane, which answers `hasToken` instead.

AuditSinkKind.description: Where an audit sink sends (#1001): syslog (RFC 5424 over TCP or TLS) or HTTP (a POST of JSON lines).

AuditSinkStatus.description: A sink and how this copy of the control plane is sending to it (#1001): entries waiting (at most 10,000), dropped since it started because the queue was full, the last sent, and the last failure.

AuditSinks.description: audit/sinks and audit/setSinks (#1001): the sinks, at most 4. In audit/setSinks, a sink with no `token` keeps the token it had at the same address.

AuditSinksState.description: What audit/sinks and audit/setSinks answer (#1001): each sink and how it is sending.

accountID.description: An added account to sign in (#840); absent for the runtime's own sign-in.

BrowserControlSettings.description: Whether agents on this machine may use the app's browser tools (browser_navigate and the rest, fill_secret, hand_to_person), and whether each lease of the browser asks a person first (#4264). Kept in <settings>/browser-control.json. Only the person's own clients may change it.

BusSealedData.description: An event's data sealed to one machine (#4825): HPKE to the sealing key the lock's addMachine names, with the associated data busdata.v1|<person>|m:<machine>|<event id>. Inside is the data and the raising machine's signature of it, so a control plane can neither read it nor make one up.

machine.description: The machine it is sealed to, by its id.

ClientPermissionMode.description: The older autoReview reads as alwaysApprove.

setBy.description: Set when the organisation's mode ceiling is below approving every request: Always Approve is refused, and no agent's requests are answered for the person.

ControlAuth.description: The peer's answer: {"auth":…} (ControlAuth.Auth). `kind` is mac, iphone, ipad, browser, host, copy or page.

capabilities.description: The capabilities this client has (#1748). None from a client older than #1748, or from a host, which says its own in machine/hello.

page.description: With a `w:<host>` identity (#1480): the port of that host's loopback listener. The socket then carries a page from the loopback origin on port <page>, whose own exchange follows the ok, bound to that origin.

publicKey.description: With an `s:<client>` identity (#995): the key of the client that signs in, X9.63. The exchange's MAC is under the ECDH of it and the control plane's key, as a paired client's is.

ControlClientChanged.description: control/clientChanged: a client paired, renamed, connected or went; nothing says list them all again.

ControlCodeShown.description: clients/startPairing, machines/startEnroll: the code, until when it works, and for a host the one line to run on the server.

ControlCutOff.description: control/cutOff (#1002, D13): to every client of a suspended person, just before the control plane closes their sockets with 4403 suspended.

ControlEndpoint.description: One place a control plane answers (R16).

ControlHello.description: The control plane's first line of the exchange: {"hello":…} (ControlAuth.Hello).

previous.description: The control plane's key before control/rotate (#997, spec 736 FR-043), for 30 days after: a member that still trusts it proves itself with it, and is given the new key in ok.

ControlInstallProgress.description: control/installProgress: a step of Add a Machine.

capabilities.description: The capabilities this host said in its last machine/hello (#1748). None from a host older than #1748.

missing.description: Of the control plane's required capabilities for hosts, the ones this host does not have (#1748). Its state is then needsUpdate.

owner.description: The user who owns the machine (#994).

ControlMoved.description: control/moved: where the control plane is now (T085).

ControlNewKey.description: The control plane's new key (#997, spec 736 FR-043), in ok to a member that proved itself with the previous one. proof is the HMAC of the new key under the member's shared key from the previous one, so only the holder of the previous key could have made it. The member trusts the new key from then on, with no new pairing.

ControlPerson.description: Who a client belongs to (#994): its person, their role, and whether they are the local owner.

ControlPush.description: The `agents` key of a push the control plane sends through APNs (#1460), beside an `aps` that says only that an agent needs the person: a ControlPushItem, sealed.

ControlPushItem.description: What a control plane's push carries, sealed whole to the device (#1460): the need, whether to buzz, and the banner's words. No headline is a withdrawal.

restartable.description: Whatever runs this control plane starts it again after control/restart (#4252): Agents Host's launch agent on a Mac. Absent where nothing would.

publicWeb.description: Where a browser anywhere opens the page, on the control plane's own domain (#1459): its https address, when it serves the page there.

publicViews.description: The origin of the sandbox proxy that draws MCP Apps views on the page at publicWeb (#1484): a second name in front of the same control plane. None when it draws no views there.

capabilities.description: The capabilities the control plane has (#1748).

joinCommand.description: The one line to run on a server so that it asks to join as this client's person, with no code (#994).

DefaultAccountRequest.description: runtimes/setDefaultAccount (#999): a runtime's account for new sessions. accountID default (or absent) is the runtime's own sign-in.

DesktopControlLiveFrame.description: The live tile's latest look at the Mac's screen while an agent holds the screen lease (#3004, US4, FR-011): a downscaled JPEG of the whole screen, base64, or, while the screen is locked, locked and no image (FR-012). Sent only to the clients showing that agent, never recorded, never replayed (FR-016).

image.description: Base64 JPEG. Absent while the screen is locked.

locked.description: The Mac's screen is locked: the tile says so and shows no picture.

narration.description: What the agent last did on the screen, in words: drive_screen's own reply, such as Clicked Save in TextEdit. Absent before its first action.

DesktopControlPause.description: An agent's drive_screen paused by the person's own touch (#3004, US3): the app it was driving, and when.

DesktopControlSettings.description: Whether agents on this Mac may drive its apps through drive_screen (#3004, FR-004), and whether each lease of the screen asks a person first (#4264). Kept in <settings>/desktop-control.json. Only the person's own clients may change it.

enabled.description: Whether drive_screen is offered: mode is ask or always. A client that sends only enabled sets always (true) or off (false).

DomainClaim.description: A claimed email domain (#1002, D8, FR-010): proved by the TXT record `txtValue` at `txtName`, for one org provider. The control plane keeps it at v1/signin/domains/<domain>.json and checks it each day; 7 days of failures take it back to notProved. `sendHere` sends an email at the domain to the provider (signIn/discover); `require` refuses a built-in sign-in at the domain to join, pair or renew (D9).

DomainClaimState.description: Whether a claimed domain's TXT record was found (#1002).

EffectiveLayerValue.description: One layer's value of a rule, from the top down (#2957, data-model.md "EffectiveLayerValue"). kept is true when the layer sets a value but a layer above it caps the effect: the value stays, and applies again when the cap goes (FR-006).

words.description: The value in the clients' words, or "Not set" when the layer does not set this rule.

EffectivePolicy.description: What a folder's agents may do, after every layer (#2957, data-model.md "EffectivePolicy"). Made by policylayers.Resolve; never stored.

behind.description: The person's machines that do not say host.policy-layers/1 (Edge Cases, "A machine of an older version").

EffectiveRule.description: The effective value of one rule, with every layer that sets it (#2957, data-model.md "EffectiveRule").

decides.description: Absent when no layer sets this rule: today's default applies.

layers.description: Every layer from the top down, for Where this comes from.

cap.description: The tightest value of the layers above the one being edited; a menu dims what is looser.

capLine.description: For example "Acme: at most Approve for me".

ElicitationSecret.description: An agent's ask_secret (#2885): one named secret, typed into a masked field. The value goes to the person's secrets.env on the host, never into the record.

canBeSessionOnly.description: The host can keep it for this session only (#3548): an answer whose content has sessionOnly true is kept for the asking session and deleted when it is archived, not saved to secrets.env. Left out by an older host.

canAskBeforeUse.description: The host keeps it with Ask before use (#4014, #4016): on unless the answer's content has needsApproval false, which the card's toggle sends. Left out by an older host, which has no such flag.

description.description: The agent's description of the secret (#4167), for the person to change on the card. The answer's content has the person's under description; left out, the secret keeps the one it has.

GitCredential.description: A credential for one git command. Never printed, logged or kept.

GitCredentialRequest.description: git/credential, git/fill (#1122): only https, and only the server. `path` is the Go host's, unread by Swift.

GitView.description: GitView (Model/AgentChanges.swift): `{ shared: { since } }`, `{ unavailable: … }` and so on.

Group.description: A group (#1761, spec 736 FR-027): everyone, or named users. It owns machine providers: only its users see them and start machines from them (FR-028).

source.description: A SCIM group's provider (#1002). Absent for a group an admin made.

role.description: Gives the admin role (#1002, FR-020): its members are admins.

GroupList.description: groups/list (#1761): every group for an admin; for a member, the groups they are in.

GroupRequest.description: groups/remove (#1761): the group. Refused while a machine provider or a bot has it.

GroupRoleSet.description: groups/setRole (#1002, FR-020): mark a SCIM group as giving the admin role, or not (no role).

GroupSet.description: groups/set (#1761): makes a group, or with id changes one. One user is a list of one.

GroupSource.description: Where a group comes from (#1002, FR-019): an org provider's SCIM. Only SCIM changes its members.

GroupsChanged.description: control/groupsChanged (#1761): a group was made, changed or removed.

policy.description: Set when the guarded file is a folder's .agents/policy.json (#2957, frame D): the rules the change makes looser, and the words for the card.

GuardedChangePolicy.description: What a waiting change to a folder's .agents/policy.json does (#2957, contracts/policy-layers-api.md): the rules it makes looser, and one line that says so, such as "Permission mode: Ask → Bypass Permissions".

was.description: The approved value's words when the change loosens one rule, for the card's Keep <was> (frame D): "Ask".

HandoverMember.description: A member as a copy says it, for the one driving a handover (Handover.Status.Member).

HandoverStatus.description: handover/status: what a copy says of itself, for the one driving a handover to check before each step (R16).

JoinDecided.description: control/joinDecided (#994): a request ended, approved or not, so every card for it goes.

JoinRequest.description: machines/joinRequests, control/joinRequested (#994): a machine waiting for approval, with the code it shows.

LocalSecret.description: A secret this machine keeps for itself (#5122): an agent saved it (ask_secret, capture_secret, generate_secret) or a connector's form set it. Every session's agent on this machine can name it. No value.

backedUp.description: Always false: a secret this machine keeps for itself is on this machine only.

needsApproval.description: Ask before use (#4014): a person approves each use (#4015). Left out is off.

description.description: A secret's description (#4167): one or two sentences on what it is and what it is for, such as which account and scopes. Not secret, and not sealed: the control plane may keep it. Never a value. Left out when it has none.

LocalSecrets.description: secrets/localList (#5122): every secret this machine keeps for itself, by name. No value.

Lock.description: A person's machine lock (#3399, specs/3399-machine-lock): its chain of entries, the root first. lock/get, and machine/lock to a machine.

LockAdd.description: lock/add (#3399): entries to put on the end of the caller's lock, in order. The first names the head as its previous; the control plane writes each with a conditional write on the head, so two entries cannot both follow one head.

LockBody.description: What a lock entry says (#3399), as its signer wrote it: the JSON that LockEntry.body carries, byte for byte. v is 1. Every entry names its person and, except the root, previous: the SHA-256 of the entry before's body. signer is the P-256 signing key that signed it, X9.63. key is the root's first signing key, the client, machine or invite added, the key removed, or the recovery key's public half. sealingKey is a machine's (addMachine); id is the machine's id (addMachine), or the client's id that the control plane knows it by (root and addClient, #3543), so a machine names the device in its audit from the lock; clientKind is a client's (addClient: mac, remote or web); expires is an invite's; sealed is a recovery entry's (#3493, D4): the recovery key's private half, AES-256-GCM under a key made from the recovery secret the person keeps (a 12-byte nonce, then the sealed 32 bytes and the tag), so a new client that is typed the secret signs with it.

LockDelivery.description: A request signed for a machine (#3492), as the control plane keeps it and delivers it: the method, the params as the sender wrote them (text, so no byte of them changes on the way), and the signature.

LockEntry.description: One entry of a machine lock (#3399): body is a LockBody's JSON, kept as the signer wrote it, so no language has to write it again the same way. sig is ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256 over "agents-lock/1\n" then body, the 64 bytes r then s (as WebCrypto and CryptoKit's rawRepresentation write it). The entry's hash is the SHA-256 of body.

LockEntryKind.description: What a lock entry changes (#3399): root names the first signing key; addClient a client's signing key; addMachine a machine's key and sealing key, signed by a signer or an invite; invite a one-use key that may add one machine; remove a client, machine or invite no longer trusted; recovery the recovery key, or a new one.

LockGet.description: lock/get (#3399): with no person, the caller's own lock. With person, that person's: only an admin may read another's (#3491), to check the machine keys an org route is sealed to (specs/3399-machine-lock D7, D8).

LockHead.description: Where a machine lock stands (#3399): how many entries it has, and head, the SHA-256 of the newest one's body. lock/add's answer, and control/lockChanged.

LockHello.description: lock/hello (#3492, specs/3399-machine-lock D6): a client opens a checked channel to a machine. key is its signing key (P-256, X9.63), which the machine's lock must name as a client; ephemeral is a new ECDH P-256 key for this channel alone; sig is ECDSA P-256 (r then s) with SHA-256 over "agents-lock-channel/1\nclient\n" then ephemeral.

LockHelloReply.description: lock/hello's answer (#3492): key is the machine's own key, which the client's lock must name as an addMachine; ephemeral is the machine's new ECDH P-256 key; sig is ECDSA with the machine's key over "agents-lock-channel/1\nmachine\n", the client's ephemeral, the machine's ephemeral, then the client's key. Each side then makes a key for each direction with HKDF-SHA256 (the ECDH secret; salt the client's then the machine's ephemeral; info "agents-lock-channel/1 client" or "… machine"), and every request and answer carries "lock":{"n":…,"mac":…} last: HMAC-SHA256 over the count (8 bytes, big-endian) then the message without that member.

LockJoin.description: lock/join (#3490, specs/3399-machine-lock D2): a client that is not in its person's lock asks to be added. key is its signing key (P-256, X9.63); commitment is the SHA-256 of "agents-lock-join/1\n", key, then a 16-byte nonce that the client shows only after a signer sent its own (lock/joinReveal), so a control plane cannot try the six digits again and again.

LockJoinDecided.description: control/lockJoinDecided (#3490): how a request to join the lock ended: approved (a signer put the client's addClient on the lock), denied or expired.

LockJoinEnd.description: lock/joinDeny (#3490): a signer says no, or the asking client gives up.

LockJoinNonce.description: lock/joinAnswer (a signer's nonce, 16 bytes, sent once) and lock/joinReveal (the asking client's nonce, which must match its commitment) (#3490).

LockJoinRequest.description: lock/joinRequests and control/lockJoinRequested (#3490): a client asking to join its person's lock, to every client of that person, and sent again in place as it goes on. client is the asking client's id, so it knows its own. nonce is the signer's, once one sent it (lock/joinAnswer), and answeredBy is that signer's client id; reveal is the asking client's nonce, once it showed it. Each screen makes the six digits from key, reveal and nonce. machine is set when a machine asks (#3491, D3): client is then the machine's id, kind is unknown, and a signer approves it with an addMachine whose key and sealing key are both key, the machine's own.

LockJoinStarted.description: lock/join's answer (#3490): the request, and when it ends unanswered.

LockSignature.description:
A request signed by its sender's own key (#3492, D6, D7): a client's kept request for a machine that is not there, or a machine's call to another of its person's machines. It goes as the request's "lock" member. sig is ECDSA P-256 (r then s) with SHA-256 over "agents-lock-request/1
", to, "
", at in decimal, "
", the method, "
", then the params as sent. to is the machine's id; a machine may leave it out for another machine it named by name. at is seconds since 1970. The machine refuses one whose key its lock does not name, older than a day, or seen before.

MachineAccountsCall.description: machine/accounts (#3967), for an agent on a machine: its person's outside accounts, after add is added (one with the same service and address goes in its place) and remove is taken out (#5253).

ops.description: What manage_accounts did to the accounts (#4157): the control plane writes an audit entry for each.

remove.description: The accounts to take out, by service and address (#5253), after add. Needs machine.accounts/2: an older control plane does not know it.

MachineJoinAsk.description: POST /v1/join (#994, spec 736 FR-017): a machine with no code asks to join. `person` names whose it is to be, by name or id; with none, an admin approves it.

MachineJoinDecision.description: GET /v1/join/<request> (#994): waiting, or how it ended; `host` once approved.

controlKey.description: Once approved: the control plane's public key, which the machine keeps as a code's would give it.

name.description: Once approved: the control plane's name.

MachineJoinTicket.description: POST /v1/join: the request, the short code the machine shows, and when it ends (10 minutes).

MachinePolicy.description: machine/policy (#998, FR-006): to a machine that says host.policy/1, on its channel 0, at each join and within 5 seconds of each change. A signed policy, or none when no policy was ever set.

MachineSecretHeld.description: One of the person's secrets that a machine holds a copy of (#4158), as it sends it with machine/secretOps: its version, its hint and its last operation there. Never the value.

hint.description: The value's last 4 characters (#4158), from a machine that holds a copy: only for a value of 16 characters or more, and a card's is the last 4 of its number. Left out otherwise. The control plane passes it to the person's own clients and never writes it to its store.

MachineSecretOpsCall.description: machine/secretOps (#4156): what a machine's agents did with its person's secrets, for the control plane's audit. At most one operation per secret, session, place and minute, with a count. held, when there, is every one of the person's secrets the machine holds a copy of (#4158), in place of what it sent before.

MachineUser.description: machine/user (#1761): to a machine on its channel 0, at each join and when its user changes. Its user, their kind, and the labels runs-on: matches (FR-034); for a bot at its cap, until when it starts no work (FR-033).

bots.description: For a person: the names of the bots in their groups (#2027). A runs-on: workflow that names one is heard here, once approved here, and its matches are sent to the control plane, never run here.

MachineUserSettings.description: machine/userSettings (#1760, FR-024, FR-025): to a machine, on its channel 0, when it joins and when its user's settings or secrets change. Sent only on the links of that user's own machines. secrets is every secret the user has that is sealed to this machine (#3397): a name missing from it was removed, or waits for the person's client to seal it.

waiting.description: The user's secrets that are not sealed to this machine yet (#4167): what list_secrets says of them. Never a value.

OrgPolicy.description: The organisation's policy (#998, spec 998 FR-001, FR-002): one document, kept by the control plane at v1/policy.json, signed by its control key and sent to every machine that says host.policy/1. Each rule is optional; an absent rule sets no ceiling. Only an admin changes it. The control plane sets version, issued, changedBy and requires; stopAll and budgets.raises change only by policy/stopAll and policy/raise.

version.description: One more at each change. A machine refuses a lower one (FR-008).

requires.description: The capabilities a machine needs to follow this policy: host.policy/1, and one for each later rule (FR-014). A machine that lacks one starts no agent.

permissionMode.description: #2957: the loosest permission level, on Auto's four levels (research R5). The control plane reads modeCeiling into this once and drops modeCeiling.

permissionRequests.description: #2957: alwaysApprove or default (Ask me), the loosest answer to a permission request.

sandbox.description: Required refuses the choice off and the states none and runtimeControlled. runtime (#2957) refuses only off. Absent is the person's choice.

runtimes.description: The runtimes allowed, by runtime id. Absent allows every runtime.

workflows.description: #2957: the most workflows on at once, in each folder.

noticeLimits.description: #2957: how many notices a burst allows, and how long to wait after one.

archiveMyChats.description: #2957: whether agents may archive the person's finished chats. false is tighter.

requireFollowing.description: The control plane refuses agent starts and prompts on a machine that has not applied this version.

groups.description: Empty. A place for later layers that only make a rule tighter.

OrgProvider.description: An org sign-in provider (#1002, D1, FR-001): an OIDC issuer that an organisation registered for this control plane. Kept at v1/signin/providers/<id>.json; its client secret is sealed beside it and never returned. The control plane sets version, secret, created, changed and redirectURI.

id.description: [a-z0-9-]{2,32}, made from the name when absent at add, never changed: the provider of each sign-in it makes.

name.description: On the button: Sign in with <name>. 1 to 40 characters.

issuer.description: An https URL. Its discovery document must name it as issuer.

accountClaim.description: The claim that names a person for life (D5): sub, or oid for Entra.

tenant.description: Entra: the tid an ID token must have.

redirectURI.description: The callback to register at the provider: this control plane's https address and /v1/oidc/callback. Only in answers.

scim.description: SCIM for this provider (slice 2a). Set by scim/set only.

OrgProviderCheck.description: signIn/orgProviders/check (#1002, FR-004): what the issuer's discovery document lacks, and how many keys its JWKS has.

OrgProviderJoin.description: Who may join through an org provider (D10): only people from SCIM, anyone the provider signs in, or only by invite.

OrgProviderKept.description: An org provider with its store tag, for an admin (#1002).

OrgProviderList.description: signIn/orgProviders/list (#1002): every org provider, for an admin. No secret.

OrgProviderPreset.description: Which form filled an org provider (#1002, research R3). Only googleWorkspace changes a check: hd must be a claimed domain.

OrgProviderSCIM.description: An org provider's SCIM (#1002, FR-013, FR-016): on or off, and the attribute that matches a provisioned person to a sign-in.

OrgProviderSecret.description: Who set an org provider's client secret, when, and its fingerprint: the first 8 hex of its SHA-256 (#1002, D4). Never the value.

OrgProviderSet.description: signIn/orgProviders/set (#1002, FR-001 to FR-004): add or change an org provider. secret is written only, never read back; needed to add. rev is the tag the admin read; none to add.

OrgRoute.description: An organisation's way to the model for one or more runtimes (#999, spec FR-001): an org key or a gateway. The control plane keeps it at v1/org/routes/<id>.json; its secrets are sealed by an admin's client to each machine and client that may hold them (#3397), in a record beside it, never in this one. The control plane sets version, secretFields, created and changed; the admin's client says fingerprint and sealVersion. machines is how many machines hold its version, and waiting how many may use it and have no copy yet, for an admin.

id.description: [a-z0-9-]{1,40}, made from the name when absent at add, never changed.

name.description: What members see, such as Acme Bedrock. 1 to 60 characters.

runtimes.description: The runtimes it serves: only those whose row of the spec's table allows the kind.

models.description: The runtime's model ids to the gateway's. Absent: the runtime's ids as they are.

groups.description: The groups whose people may use it (T1). Empty: everyone.

defaultFor.description: The runtimes whose default account it is.

secretFields.description: The names of the secret fields that are set (apiKey, awsAccessKeyId, serviceAccount, entraClientSecret, …), never a value.

fingerprint.description: The first 8 hex of SHA-256 of each secret value (spec D14), by field, as the admin's client worked it out.

machines.description: How many machines said they keep this version (machine/orgRoutesApplied). Only in orgRoutes/list.

sealVersion.description: One more each time the secrets, the kind, the vendor or the settings change: what each secret's associated data binds (#3397). 0 with no secret.

waiting.description: How many machines may use the route and have no copy of its secrets yet: they wait for an admin's client to seal it for them (#3397). Only in orgRoutes/list.

OrgRouteCheck.description: orgRoutes/check (#999, #3397): what one small request from a machine that holds the route found, in words.

OrgRouteDelivery.description: machine/orgRoutes (#999): every route the machine's person (or bot) may use. An empty list removes every route.

OrgRouteKept.description: An org route with its store tag, for an admin (#999).

OrgRouteKind.description: How an org route reaches the model (#999): an org key of the runtime's own vendor, or a gateway: Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, Microsoft Azure, or the organisation's own base URL.

OrgRouteMine.description: A route the caller may use (#999): no settings, no fingerprint.

waiting.description: One of the caller's machines may use it and waits for an admin's client to seal it (#3397).

OrgRouteRecipientsRequest.description: orgRoutes/recipients (#3397): the groups the route is for; none for everyone.

OrgRouteReplaceKey.description: orgRoutes/replaceKey (#999, #3397): new values for every one of a route's secret fields, sealed by the client.

OrgRouteRequest.description: orgRoutes/check and orgRoutes/remove (#999): a route, and for remove the tag the admin read.

OrgRouteSealed.description: An org route's secrets as an admin's client sealed them (#3397, specs/3397-client-sealing): every field, to every recipient of orgRoutes/recipients. Each envelope is HPKE to the recipient's key, info com.alexecollins.agents.orgroute.v3, associated data orgroute.v3|<route id>|<recipient>|<field>|<sealVersion>|<kind>|<vendor or empty>|<hex SHA-256 of the settings, one name=value line each>.

sealVersion.description: The kept sealVersion plus one; 1 for a route with no secret yet.

fingerprint.description: The first 8 hex of SHA-256 of each value, by field.

values.description: By recipient (m:<machine id> or c:<client id>), then by field.

OrgRouteSet.description: orgRoutes/set (#999, #3397): add a route, or change one. sealed carries every secret, sealed by the client; it is needed when the secrets, the kind, the vendor or the settings change, and absent keeps the secrets as they are. rev is the tag the admin read; none to add.

OrgRouteSettings.description: An org route's settings that are not secret (#999, data-model.md). bedrock: region. vertex: folder, location. azure: resource or address, apiVersion, and tenant and clientID for an Entra app. baseURL: address, and header, the header the key goes in.

OrgRouteStamp.description: Who changed an org route, and when (#999).

OrgRouteVendor.description: An org route's vendor (#999): whose key a key route holds, and the API shape of a base-URL or Azure route.

OrgRouteVersion.description: A route a machine keeps, and its version (#999).

OrgRoutesApplied.description: machine/orgRoutesApplied (#999): the routes a machine keeps, after a delivery.

OrgRoutesLeft.description: control/orgRoutesLeft (#999): a machine was removed with these routes on it. To its person and to every admin.

OutsideAccount.description: Settings ▸ You ▸ Accounts (#3967): one outside account of the person's (gitlab.com, AWS, Slack…). It holds no secret: card and secret are the names of secrets in Settings ▸ You ▸ Secrets, or where one is.

service.description: The service, as its address: gitlab.com, aws.amazon.com.

description.description: What it is for and who uses it, in one or two sentences, so an agent can tell it from the other accounts of the same service (#4164). Absent on an account made before it: the clients say No description.

address.description: The address it signs in with.

username.description: The user name it signs in with, when that is not the address (#5116). Plain text, never a secret. Absent when not set.

monthlyCostUsd.description: What it costs a month, in US dollars. Absent when not known.

card.description: The card it bills, by its name in Settings ▸ You ▸ Secrets. Never the number.

secret.description: Its token or key, by its name in Settings ▸ You ▸ Secrets or where it is. Never the value.

twoFactor.description: TOTP, passkey, SMS, or absent for none.

issue.description: The issue that made it: #12 or owner/repo#12.

made.description: The date it was made, YYYY-MM-DD.

edited.description: When it was last changed (#4157): the control plane sets it when an account takes another's place, by manage_accounts or a client's Edit… (#4160). made stays. Absent for one never changed.

lastOp.description: Its newest operation (#4157): a read or change by manage_accounts, or a read of the secret or card it names, as the machine that answers knows it. The control plane does not store it: it keeps the newest the machines said in memory and puts it on user/settings (#4160), and drops one a client sends.

tokenExpires.description: The date its token expires, YYYY-MM-DD.

notes.description: Where the password is, the account's name and the like. Never a secret.

projects.description: The projects that use it, by name. Absent or empty: all of them.

addedBy.description: The session whose manage_accounts add made it (#5253): an agent may remove such an account with no card; one with none is the person's, and its removal asks them. The control plane keeps it from the add that made it, and keeps it through a change by an agent or a client. Absent for one a person added, or one made before it.

askBeforeUse.description: Ask before use (#4163): an agent's manage_accounts get of it waits on a person's approval, as a secret's use does (#4015). Absent is on, also for an account an agent adds; false is off, which a person sets, or Always Approve on its request does. Not sealed: kept with the account, and agentsd enforces it.

OutsideAccounts.description: The accounts part of the person's settings (#3967), and machine/accounts' answer.

PermissionLevel.description: Plan: reads and plans, changes nothing; Ask: asks before it changes things; Approve for me: does not ask for normal changes in its folder; Bypass Permissions: never asks, even for a change outside its folder (#2658, #2864).

PersonInvite.description: people/invite (#994): the new person's name and role.

PersonInvited.description: people/invite: the invite code to send, for one use within 7 days. Its first client pairs as the new person.

PersonKeyRotation.description: The person key moving to a new pair (#2957, data-model.md "PersonKeyRotation"): the new public key, signed by the one it replaces. A machine moves its pin only with one that checks against the key it has pinned.

PersonMachine.description: A machine in People: its name, its state and nothing inside it (FR-019).

PersonRemovePreview.description: people/removePreview (FR-029, #1763): what Remove would take, for the admin to confirm. Started machines are stopped and deleted through their providers, each with the work on it that is not pushed; registered machines leave the control plane.

PersonRoleRequest.description: people/setRole (#994). Refused when it would leave no admin.

PersonRow.description: people/list (#994): a user, with their clients and machines.

spentTodayUSD.description: A bot's spend today, UTC, as its machines reported it (#1761).

scim.description: What SCIM says of the person, for one SCIM made (#1002). Shown as Managed by <provider>.

provisioned.description: Made by SCIM and not signed in yet: Waiting for first sign-in (#1002).

suspended.description: Suspended by their org provider (#1002, D13).

roleFrom.description: The SCIM groups that give the person their role (#1002, FR-020): Set by <provider>. Absent: set by hand.

PersonSCIM.description: What an org provider's SCIM says of a person (#1002, FR-015). The match is only inside its provider.

PersonSettings.description: What agents call the person, and their pronouns (#121), as given: person.json in the person's settings.

PersonSuspended.description: Why a person is suspended (#1002, D13): by SCIM, by a refresh the provider refused (Q1 A), or by an admin's id; with the provider and when.

PinnedPersonKey.description: The person's public key this machine trusts (#2957, data-model.md "PinnedPersonKey"), kept at <root>/person-key.pub.json: from a join code, the Mac window's direct link, or, for a machine joined before this version, the first signed layer the control plane sends (trust on first use, research R3).

PolicyApplied.description: machine/policyApplied (#998): a machine kept this version of the policy.

PolicyApplyYoursResult.description: policy/applyYours's result (#2957): the revision now applied here.

PolicyAskForMore.description: policy/askForMore (#3262, spec 998 FR-019): a person at their organisation's budget asks an admin to raise it for today.

PolicyBehindMachine.description: A machine of the person's that does not say host.policy-layers/1 (#2957, EffectivePolicy.behind, Edge Cases "A machine of an older version").

PolicyEffectiveRequest.description: policy/effective (#2957): the rules for an agent in folder, or, with no folder, outside any folder layer.

PolicyEnvironment.description: The variable names a person's own pass-through list may name (#998, FR-011a), * at the end allowed. runtimes names ones for one runtime only (#2957, moved here from runtime-environment.json's own runtimes map).

PolicyFolderRequest.description: policy/folder (#2957): the folder's own layer, from .agents/policy.json.

PolicyFolderState.description: policy/folder's result (#2957, data-model.md "A folder's layer"): the approved copy, and a waiting change when one is pending.

invalid.description: Why the file on disk cannot be read as a layer (not JSON, or a value out of range), when that is why a change is pending.

PolicyFolderWithRules.description: One folder that sets its own rules, for the Agents ▸ Policy banner (#2957, EffectivePolicy.foldersWithRules).

PolicyHelpers.description: The ceiling over each folder's helper limits (#998, #64).

PolicyKeeper.description: Which machine signs your layer (#2957, research R4): the Mac's host, or the first machine of yours that saved one, when you have no Mac.

PolicyKept.description: policy/get and policy/set (#998): the whole policy with its store tag, for an admin. No policy and no rev when none was ever set. machines is each machine's applied version, by host id.

PolicyLayerRef.description: Which layer sets or decides a rule (#2957, data-model.md "PolicyLayerRef"): the organisation, the person ("You"), or a folder.

name.description: The organisation's name, "You", or the folder's name.

folder.description: The folder's path, when kind is folder.

PolicyRaiseRequest.description: policy/raise (#998): an admin raises a person's budget for today (UTC).

PolicyReach.description: A way a runtime reaches the model (#999): the person's own sign-in, an org key, or a gateway.

PolicyRefusal.description: The data of a policyRefused error (#998, FR-010): why, the rule, and the words for the client. layer and value name which layer decided and what it allows (#2957, R8): "Acme: at most Approve for me".

PolicyRefuseMore.description: policy/refuseMore (#3262), an admin's: refuse an Ask for More. policy/raise with the request's id raises it.

PolicyRuleLine.description: One rule a layer sets, in the Policy pane's words (#3230): for example Per day: $40.00 a day.

PolicyRuleName.description: One rule a policy layer can set (#2957, data-model.md "EffectiveRule").

PolicyRules.description: The rules a layer sets (#2957, data-model.md "PolicyRules"): the same shape on the organisation, your and a folder's layer (FR-002). Every field is optional: absent sets nothing.

runtimes.description: A runtime not named is not allowed. Absent allows every runtime and model.

connectorTools.description: The level of each connector's tools, by the connector's name (#4099). A tool no layer names is ask when it writes and allow when it only reads.

PolicyRuntimeRule.description: One allowed runtime in a policy (#998).

models.description: The model ids allowed, with * at the end allowed (claude-sonnet-*). Absent allows every model.

reach.description: The ways this runtime may reach the model (#999). Absent: every way. [orgKey, gateway] is the org path only.

PolicySet.description: policy/set (#998): the rules, and the rev the admin read. No rev when there was no policy. Refused changedElsewhere when another admin saved first.

PolicySetBy.description: The mark on a choice a policy refuses or caps (#998, FR-010). layer names which layer decided (#2957, R8).

PolicySignature.description: The control key's signature of a policy (#998, FR-004), kept at v1/policy.sig: ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256 (es256), over the policy's canonical JSON (keys sorted, no spaces). sig is the 64 bytes r then s.

keyID.description: The first 8 bytes of the SHA-256 of the control key's X9.63 public key, base64url.

PolicyState.description: daemon/policyState and daemon/policyStateChanged (#998, T027): the organisation's policy as this machine follows it, so a client on the direct path draws the strip and the Policy pane. No version when this machine has no policy.

policy.description: The rules in force here, with only this machine's person's raises.

stopAll.description: The kill switch is on: this machine stops its turns and starts no work.

noPolicy.description: This machine had a policy from its organisation and has none it can trust now (missing, or it fails the signature check). It starts no work until it gets one.

update.description: The capabilities the policy requires that this machine lacks (FR-014). It starts no work.

refusal.description: Why this machine starts no work now, when it starts none.

PolicyStopAll.description: The kill switch (#998, FR-015): while on, every machine stops its turns and starts no work.

PolicyStopAllRequest.description: policy/stopAll (#998): the kill switch on or off, with an optional note.

PolicyView.description: policy/mine and control/policyChanged (#998): the policy in force, for any person, with only their own budget raises. No policy when none was ever set.

PolicyWorkflows.description: How many workflows a layer allows turned on at once, in each folder (#2957). Unset means 20.

ProjectsJoined.description: projects/joined (#2317): a machine's folders and the project each names, all of them each time.

ProviderGroup.description: providers/setGroup (#1761): the group whose users may use the provider. No group is the admins' alone.

ProviderSecretsKeep.description: providers/keepSecrets (#3398): secrets for a provider the machine carries, laid over what it has in ~/.agents-secrets; an empty value takes one away. The control plane passes them on and keeps none.

ReadAPI.description: readApi/list (#2019), an admin's: the read API's tokens, newest first, revoked ones too; its URL; and the OTLP exporter when one is set.

ReadToken.description: A read API token (#2019, #1804 decision 4), with no value: the control plane keeps only its SHA-256. It reads the organisation's reports at /v1/read/reports, and nothing else.

ReadTokenMade.description: readApi/make (#2019): the token, its value once (never shown again), and the URL to read.

ReadTokenMake.description: readApi/make (#2019): a name for the token, such as the BI tool that uses it.

ReadTokenRevoke.description: readApi/revoke (#2019): the token to stop at once.

RequestSecretUse.description: A use of a secret with Ask before use (#4015), waiting on a person: its kind is approve. It names the secret, never its value, and where agentsd puts the value.

place.description: Where the value goes: the page's domain for a fill, owner/repo for CI, the server's name for an MCP server, for terminal the name of the command that ran agents-secret, as that command says it, and for account the account's id, as manage_accounts list gives it.

call.description: For account (#4163): the manage_accounts call that waits, such as get. name is then the account's service and address.

app.description: For screen (#4264): the app drive_screen names in the call that asks.

digest.description: For connector (#4538): the server's entry digest when the agent asked. Approve approves only that entry: one changed since is refused, and the agent asks again.

sessionOnly.description: The secret is the session's own (#3548): Always Approve is the same as Approve for This Session.

needsSignature.description: The machine is Linux (#4058): the value opens only with the release key its control plane keeps, which the control plane gives only for an approval the person's client signed. An answer that allows the use carries approval; one without it is refused.

RequestSecretUseAnswer.description: A person's answer to a secret's use (#4015). once allows this use; session every use at this place until the session ends or is archived; always adds a grant for this place, for every session; hour (terminal only, #4179) allows every call of agents-secret NAME with no session's grant for one hour, kept in agentsd's memory only; deny refuses it. A terminal's use takes once, hour or deny. Only the control and device roles answer.

approval.description: The answering client's signature of its answer (#4058), required when the request says needsSignature and the action is not deny: method secrets/approveUse, params the JSON text {"request":<the request's id>,"name","use","place","action"} as the request names them, and a LockSignature to this machine by the client's lock key. The machine checks it against its lock and sends it to the control plane, which gives the release key only for a fresh one it has not seen.

RetentionSetRequest.description: retention/set. Without confirmed, a change that would delete agents at once is only described.

RuntimeSignIn.description: Whether a runtime is signed in on the machine itself (#3349), for one a client signs in there with no browser on the machine: Claude and Codex on a server. Absent on a Mac, which signs its runtimes in in Runtimes.

relayed.description: A Mac lends it its own sign-in (056), so it runs without one of its own.

RuntimeSignInFinish.description: The end of a sign-in runtimes/signInStart began (#3349): the code the sign-in page gave, when the step wants one, or cancel to stop it.

RuntimeSignInKey.description: An API key to sign a runtime in with on the machine (#3349), when there is no account to sign in to.

RuntimeSignInStep.description: What the person does to sign a runtime in on a machine with no browser (#3349): open url in a browser of their own, then type userCode there (Codex), or paste back the code the page gives (wantsCode, Claude).

userCode.description: The code to type on the page at url.

wantsCode.description: The page gives a code to paste back with runtimes/signInFinish.

SCIMEmail.description: A SCIM user's email (RFC 7643 §4.1.2), to show only: never a sign-in.

SCIMMatch.description: Which SCIM attribute must equal an org sign-in's account claim for the two to be one person (#1002, D5, R5).

SCIMName.description: A SCIM user's name parts (RFC 7643 §4.1.1), kept as they came.

SCIMSet.description: scim/set (#1002): turn SCIM on or off for an org provider, and say which attribute matches a sign-in (externalId by default).

SCIMToken.description: A SCIM bearer token of one org provider (#1002, D12, FR-014), with no value: the control plane keeps only its SHA-256.

SCIMTokenList.description: scim/tokens/list (#1002): one provider's tokens, newest first, revoked ones too.

SCIMTokenMade.description: scim/tokens/make (#1002): the token, its value once (never shown again), and the SCIM base URL to give the provider.

SCIMTokenMake.description: scim/tokens/make (#1002): a name for the token, and when it ends, if ever. Refused while two are live.

SCIMTokenUse.description: When and from where a SCIM token was last used (#1002, D12), written at most once a minute.

setBy.description: Set when the organisation's policy requires the command sandbox (#998): off is refused, and a runtime that cannot be put in a sandbox does not start.

SealRecipient.description: A machine or a client to seal a secret to (#3397): its id as the associated data names it (m:<machine id> or c:<client id>), its name, and its P-256 key, X9.63. The control plane gives the key, and a client checks a machine's against the sealing key of that machine's addMachine in its person's lock before it seals to it (#3491, specs/3399-machine-lock D8), so a control plane cannot give one of its own. owner is the person whose machine it is, so an admin's client knows whose lock to read; none for a client recipient.

SealRecipients.description: orgRoutes/recipients and user/secretRecipients (#3397). user is, for user/secretRecipients, the person whose secret it is, as its associated data names them.

SealedEnvelope.description: Envelope: HPKE (P-256, HKDF-SHA256, AES-256-GCM) to one device's key. Nothing in it is legible but to that device.

SealedUserSecret.description: One secret in machine/userSettings (#3397): sealed to this machine by its person's client.

needsApproval.description: Ask before use (#4014), as the person's client sealed it: the associated data ends |ask when it is on, so a flag the control plane changed does not open. Left out is off.

description.description: A secret's description (#4167): one or two sentences on what it is and what it is for, such as which account and scopes. Not secret, and not sealed: the control plane may keep it. Never a value. Left out when it has none.

SealingAddItem.description: One item of sealing/add (#3397): new copies at the item's version, by recipient, then by field.

SealingItem.description: sealing/work and orgRoutes/sealed (#3397): a secret the calling client holds a copy of, and the recipients that have none. id is the route's id or the secret's name; user is the person whose secret it is. kind, vendor and settings are the route's, to make the associated data; a copy opens only if they are what the admin sealed. mine is the client's copy by field (a person's secret has the one field value).

needsApproval.description: Ask before use (#4014), for a person's secret: the associated data of every copy ends |ask, so the client opens its own copy and seals the missing ones with it (#4016). Left out is off.

SecretGrant.description: A place where a person allowed a secret with Ask before use always (#4015): a use there does not ask.

place.description: The page's domain for a fill, owner/repo for CI, the server's name for an MCP server.

SecretGrantChange.description: secrets/addGrant and secrets/removeGrant (#4015): a person allows a secret with Ask before use always at a place, or takes that away. Only the control and device roles reach them.

SecretGrants.description: secrets/grants (#4015): every grant of this machine's secrets with Ask before use.

SecretLastOp.description: A secret's last operation (#4158): what it was, when, and the session that did it, the newest any machine reported. No place, no value.

agent.description: The session that did it, so the person's own clients can name it beside a recent read. Left out for a change no session made.

SecretLeftOn.description: A machine that was removed with a secret on it (#1760, FR-026): change the secret where it was issued.

name.description: The machine's name when it was removed.

SecretNeedsApprovalRequest.description: secrets/setNeedsApproval (#4014): a person turns Ask before use on or off for a secret of this machine's secrets.env, or for one session's (agentID). On takes the value out of the plain file and seals it to this machine; off puts it back. The flag of a secret of the person's (Settings ▸ You ▸ Secrets) is its client's to seal, so it is refused here.

SecretOperation.description: One read or change of a secret on a machine (#4156). Never the value, never its hint: only the name, and where it went.

place.description: Where it went: the field's domain (fill), owner/repo (ci), the server's name (mcp, env), session (env, as a session's own variable), or agents-secret (command).

agent.description: The session that read it. Left out for a change no session made.

at.description: When; for a count, the first in its minute.

count.description: How many times in the minute from at, when more than one.

SecretOperationUse.description: How a secret was read (#4156): fill (fill_secret), ci (set_ci_secret), mcp (an HTTP MCP server's header or url, through agentsd, #4120), env (given to a session at its start: its own secrets as variables, or an MCP server's ${NAME} from secrets.env) or command (agents-secret NAME, printed for a session's own command, #4178, or for a call with no session's grant that a person allowed, with the place terminal, #4179).

SecretOperationWhat.description: What an operation on a secret was (#4156): read (an agent's use of it), denied (a person denied a use with Ask before use), or added, replaced or removed.

SecretRelease.description: machine/secretRelease (#4058): a Linux machine asks its control plane to open the release layer of one value with Ask before use, for a person's signed approval. encapsulated is the HPKE encapsulated key the machine sealed the value's key with (DHKEM X25519, HKDF-SHA256, AES-256-GCM, info agents-secret-release/1); the control plane answers with the 32 bytes exported with the context "sealedsecret.release.v1|" then name. It never sees the value, which is also sealed to the machine's key.

SecretReleaseKey.description: machine/secretKey (#4058): the public half of this machine's release key, X25519, 32 bytes. The control plane makes the key pair the first time a machine asks, keeps the private half sealed by its keeper, and gives it to nobody.

SecretReleased.description: The answer to machine/secretRelease (#4058): the key that opens the release layer of one value, which the machine uses once and does not keep.

SecretTerminalRequest.description: secrets/terminalValue (#4179): agents-secret NAME with no session's grant, such as from a terminal.

command.description: The name of the command that ran agents-secret, as it says it: the request's place. agentsd cannot check it.

SecretTerminalValue.description: secrets/terminalValue's answer: the value, when a person allowed it; else the open request it waits on, and the words to say while it waits. A denied call is an error.

SecretUse.description: What agentsd does with a secret with Ask before use (#4015): fill types it into a page (fill_secret), ci sends it to GitHub (set_ci_secret), mcp adds it to an HTTP MCP server's header or URL on each request agentsd sends the server for a session (#4120). terminal (#4179) prints a secret that does not ask to `agents-secret NAME` run with no session's grant, such as from a terminal: agentsd cannot tell that caller from an agent that dropped its grant. account (#4163) is not a secret's use: manage_accounts reads an account with Ask before use; the request names the account, and Always Approve turns its Ask before use off. browser and screen (#4264) are not a secret's use either: an agent's lease of the browser or the screen on a machine whose Browser or Desktop control is ask; name is the browser or the screen, place the machine, app the app drive_screen names, and Always Approve sets the setting to always. workflow and connector (#4538) are not a secret's use either: an agent asks to turn on a workflow of its folder that is the person's to turn on (manage_workflows enable), or to approve a server waiting in its folder's .agents/mcp.json (manage_connectors approve); name is the workflow's id or the server's name, place the folder's name, digest the server's entry as the agent saw it. Their answers are once (Approve: agentsd makes the change as the person) and deny.

SecretsLeft.description: control/secretsLeft (#1760, FR-026): to the person's own clients, when one of their machines was removed with secrets on it.

SessionSecret.description: A secret kept for one session only (#3548): only that session's agent can use it (fill_secret, its environment, its MCP servers), and its host deletes it when the session is archived. No value.

title.description: The session's title, as the session list shows it.

created.description: When the name was first set for the session (#4158); a new value does not change it.

hint.description: The value's last 4 characters (#4158), from a machine that holds a copy: only for a value of 16 characters or more, and a card's is the last 4 of its number. Left out otherwise. The control plane passes it to the person's own clients and never writes it to its store.

backedUp.description: Always false (#4158): a secret for one session is on this machine only.

needsApproval.description: Ask before use (#4014): its value is sealed in the session's file, never there as plain text, and a person approves each use (#4015).

description.description: A secret's description (#4167): one or two sentences on what it is and what it is for, such as which account and scopes. Not secret, and not sealed: the control plane may keep it. Never a value. Left out when it has none.

SessionSecretRemoveRequest.description: secrets/sessionRemove (#3548): take one session's secret out now.

SessionSecretSetRequest.description: secrets/sessionSet (#3548): set a secret for one session that is not archived. The value is one line.

needsApproval.description: Ask before use (#4014): kept sealed, and a person approves each use (#4015). Left out is off.

description.description: A secret's description (#4167): one or two sentences on what it is and what it is for, such as which account and scopes. Not secret, and not sealed: the control plane may keep it. Never a value. Left out when it has none.

SessionSecrets.description: secrets/sessionList (#3548): every secret this machine keeps for one session only, by session title then name. No value.

SetClientPermissionRequest.description: An agent's own answer to permission requests (#2658, FR-019); no mode follows Settings.

SetFolderPolicyRequest.description: policy/setFolder (#2957): writes .agents/policy.json in a stable order and approves it. A value looser than the person's own effective value is kept, and the result shows it capped.

SetYourPolicyRequest.description: policy/setYours (#2957): the rules to save as your layer, at the revision this client last read. Refused conflict when revision is not the current one, notKeeper on a machine that is not the keeper, forbidden from the agent socket role, an MCP tool or a workflow (FR-010), and invalid when the rules fail policylayers.Validate.

SettleUntrustedYourPolicyRequest.description: policy/settleUntrustedYours (#3230): what the person chose for the untrusted copy in file, read at revision of your layer. sign true signs its rules with this machine's person key as the next revision of your layer; false sets the copy aside and changes nothing. Either way it is not shown again. Refused conflict when file or revision is not the current one, notKeeper on a machine that is not the keeper, forbidden from the agent socket role, an MCP tool or a workflow (FR-010), and invalid when the rules fail policylayers.Validate.

SignIn.description: One way a person signs in (#994, spec 736): `local` is the local owner's (codes, with the control plane's key), `code` an invite code redeemed; Google, Apple and GitHub come with #995.

SignInAdd.description: signIn/addToMe (#995, FR-005): a sign-in to add to the caller's person: an ID token made with signIn/providers' nonce, or a GitHub user access token.

SignInAsk.description: signIn/ask, on an `s:` connection (#2097): a browser pairs by approval. `account` is the email or GitHub login of one of the person's sign-ins; `name` is the browser's.

SignInConfigure.description: signIn/configure (#995, admins): turn a provider on or off, and set Google's allowed Workspace domains or GitHub's allowed organisations. What is left out stays as it was.

SignInDecide.description: signIn/approve, signIn/deny (#995). `code` is the code a browser shows, typed by the person: signIn/approve of a browser's request needs it (#2097).

SignInDecided.description: control/signInDecided (#995): how a request ended: approved, denied or expired.

SignInDiscover.description: signIn/discover (#1002, FR-011): the email a person typed.

SignInDiscovered.description: signIn/discover's answer: the org provider of a claimed domain that sends people there, or none. The same for an unknown domain and a domain with no switch.

SignInDomainClaim.description: signIn/domains/claim (#1002): a domain for one org provider.

SignInDomainList.description: signIn/domains/list (#1002): every claimed domain, for an admin.

SignInDomainPreview.description: signIn/domains/preview (#1002, FR-012): the people and the built-in sign-ins that Require would refuse.

SignInDomainPreviewPerson.description: A person that Require changes, with their sign-ins at the domain.

SignInDomainSet.description: signIn/domains/set (#1002, D8): a claimed domain's switches; an absent one stays. Either needs a proved domain.

SignInOrgProvider.description: An org provider on the sign-in screen (#1002, FR-003): its id, name and order, and nothing more.

SignInOrgStart.description: signIn/orgStart (#1002, D2): start an org provider's flow for this connection: pair (an `s:` connection) or addToMe (a paired client's). returnTo says where the browser comes back: agents://oidc (app) or the web page (web).

SignInOrgStarted.description: signIn/orgStart's answer: the /v1/oidc/start address to open in the browser. It ends after 10 minutes.

SignInPair.description: signIn/pair, on an `s:` connection (#995): the client's name and kind, and its provider's token: an ID token for google and apple, a user access token for github. The control plane checks it and forgets it (FR-008, FR-010).

SignInProvider.description: One sign-in provider (#995, spec 736 FR-004): google, apple or github. `on` is the admin's switch; `available` is false when this build has no client id for it, with `why`. `clientID` is the app's own, what a client signs in with (FR-012).

SignInProviders.description: signIn/providers, signIn/configure (#995): the providers. `challenge` (base64url) is what a client's nonce is made from on this connection: the hello's nonce on an `s:` connection, or a fresh one used once on a paired client's. The client makes the nonce itself, from the control key it trusts and the challenge (R2), so a token cannot be passed on to another control plane (FR-008, FR-011). `domains` (Google Workspace) and `organisations` (GitHub) are for admins only (FR-006). `orgProviders` are the org providers turned on, in order (#1002), first on every sign-in screen.

discover.description: A claimed domain sends people to its org provider: a client offers Use an Email (#1002, FR-011).

SignInRemove.description: signIn/removeFromMe (#995): an outside sign-in to take off the caller's person. The local owner's stays.

SignInRequest.description: signIn/requests, control/signInRequested (#995, FR-010): a new client that signed in with GitHub, waiting for Approve on one of the person's clients, with the code it shows. A browser's (provider `browser`, #2097) has the account typed as `login` and an empty `code`: the person types the code the browser shows.

SignInTicket.description: signIn/ticket (#1002, D3, FR-006): the ticket the callback gave, on the connection that started the flow, within 2 minutes, once. To pair, the client's name and kind too.

SignInTicketResult.description: signIn/ticket's answer: the client paired, or the sign-in added to the caller's person.

SignInWaiting.description: control/signInWaiting, on an `s:` connection (#995, FR-010): a GitHub sign-in waits for Approve on another client of the person, which shows the same code.

SignedPolicy.description: A policy and its signature (#998): what a machine receives and keeps in <root>/policy.json.

SignedYourPolicy.description: Your layer, signed by the person key (#2957, data-model.md "SignedYourPolicy"): what the control plane stores and forwards, and what a non-keeper machine verifies before it applies a copy.

policy.description: The exact CanonicalJSON bytes of YourPolicy, base64.

rotation.description: Present only on the first copy after a new person key.

key.description: #2957, research R3: the person key's public half (X9.63), so a machine that has not pinned one yet can check the signature and pin it (trust on first use) or match it against a join code's key. Sent every time; cheap, and no secret.

TeamPerson.description: people/forViews (#2951): one person or bot on this control plane, as the github, gitlab, linear and jira servers' feeding tools are fed it in their call's _meta, so a row can name them and Team can be told from Others.

jiraLogin.description: Their Jira login (#3313): the Atlassian account's email, account id or display name.

forgejoLogin.description: Their Forgejo login (#3836): their user name on the connected Forgejo or Gitea.

bitbucketLogin.description: Their Bitbucket login (#3853): their Bitbucket nickname.

azureDevOpsLogin.description: Their Azure DevOps login (#3853): their sign-in email or display name in the Azure DevOps organization.

UntrustedYourPolicy.description: A copy of your layer on disk that fails the signature check (#3230): signed with a person key this machine does not have, such as on another Mac before the root moved here. Shown, never applied, until the person signs it again here (policy/settleUntrustedYours).

file.description: The kept file's name in the settings folder: policy-yours.json, or policy-yours.json.untrusted-<time> once a change here kept it aside (#3122).

keeper.description: The host id of the machine that signed it.

keyID.description: The id of the person key it was signed with.

lines.description: Each rule the copy sets, in the Policy pane's words and order.

UserAgentConfig.description: Legacy agentConfig snapshot (#1760); new agent configuration uses per-file state in AgentConfigFiles (#2129).

UserPartHere.description: settings/userPart's answer (#1760): this machine's own part, for a client to set at the user scope with Use This Mac's. An MCP server with a token in clear is refused, so no secret goes into the user settings unsealed.

leftOut.description: What could not be taken, by name: a skill with files beside its SKILL.md.

UserPartRequest.description: settings/userPart (#1760): a part of the user settings, as this machine has it now.

UserRole.description: A user's role (#994, spec 736 FR-001): an admin manages people; a member sees only their own.

UserSealedSecret.description: user/sealedSecret's answer (#5114): this client's own envelope of the secret, as the person's client sealed it (#3397). HPKE, info com.alexecollins.agents.usersecret.v1, associated data usersecret.v1|<person id>|c:<CLIENT UUID>|<name>|<version>, with |ask at the end when needsApproval is on. The control plane never has the value.

needsApproval.description: Ask before use (#4014), bound into the associated data. Left out is off.

UserSealedSecretAccount.description: user/sealedSecret (#5114): the account a reveal or a copy was opened from, for the audit entry: its service and the address it signs in with. Never a value.

UserSealedSecretPart.description: A card's part (#3531), for a copy of one part of a card: the card number, the expiry, the CVC, the name on card or the billing ZIP.

UserSealedSecretPurpose.description: Why a person's client asks for its copy of a secret (#5114): to show it, or to put it on the clipboard. Only for the audit entry's words.

UserSealedSecretRequest.description: user/sealedSecret (#5112, #5114): a person's own client asks for its own sealed copy of one of the person's secrets, to reveal or copy it. The control plane writes the audit entry first, with the name and never the value.

part.description: A card's part, for a copy of that part; left out otherwise.

account.description: The account the secret was opened from; left out when it was opened from Secrets.

UserSecret.description: user/setSecret (#1760, FR-025): a secret the control plane keeps sealed, and sends only to its person's own machines. The value is never sent back to a client.

UserSecretAbout.description: What a machine knows of one of its user's secrets that it has no copy of yet (#4167). Never a value.

UserSecretKind.description: What a secret holds, when it is more than one value (#3531). card: a payment card that has a spend limit (locked to a merchant or category is recommended; Privacy.com or the same), as one JSON object of number, expiry (MM/YY), cvc, name and zip. fill_secret fills it a part at a time. Left out for a plain value.

UserSecretName.description: A secret's name, as ${NAME} in mcp.json and NAME= in ~/.agents-secrets/secrets.env.

UserSecretRow.description: One row of user/secretNames (#1760): a secret's name, never its value.

machines.description: The machines it was sent to.

created.description: When the name was first set (#4158); Replace… does not change it. Left out for one set before it was kept.

hint.description: The value's last 4 characters (#4158), from a machine that holds a copy: only for a value of 16 characters or more, and a card's is the last 4 of its number. Left out otherwise. The control plane passes it to the person's own clients and never writes it to its store.

backedUp.description: False when one copy only opens (#4158): machines has one and waiting is empty.

leftOn.description: Machines removed with it on them, since it was last set.

waiting.description: The person's machines that have no copy yet: they wait for one of the person's clients to seal it (#3397).

needsApproval.description: Ask before use (#4014), as the person's client last sealed it. The machines check it: the associated data binds it.

description.description: A secret's description (#4167): one or two sentences on what it is and what it is for, such as which account and scopes. Not secret, and not sealed: the control plane may keep it. Never a value. Left out when it has none.

UserSecretSet.description: user/setSecret (#1760, FR-025, #3397): a secret as the person's client sealed it to each recipient of user/secretRecipients, info com.alexecollins.agents.usersecret.v1, associated data usersecret.v1|<person id>|<recipient>|<name>|<version>. version is above the kept one: the kept one plus one, or for a name the client has none of, the time in milliseconds, above a removed one's. The control plane never has the value.

needsApproval.description: Ask before use (#4014): when on, every envelope's associated data ends |ask (usersecret.v1|<person id>|<recipient>|<name>|<version>|ask), so the control plane cannot change it. Left out is off, and the associated data is as before.

description.description: A secret's description (#4167): one or two sentences on what it is and what it is for, such as which account and scopes. Not secret, and not sealed: the control plane may keep it. Never a value. Left out when it has none.

UserSettings.description: user/settings (#1760, #2410): the person's settings that follow them to each of their machines. An omitted part has no value yet, but does not make that setting machine-local. The control plane does not read inside a part.

agentConfigFiles.description: Per-file agent configuration state (#2129), with tombstones and logical timestamps.

notifications.description: The person's notice limits (#2859), as a NoticeLimits.

accounts.description: The person's outside accounts (#3967), as an OutsideAccounts. The control plane refuses one with a value that looks like a secret.

timeZone.description: The person's time zone (#4818), as a UserTimeZone. Their Mac sets it from its own clock; a workflow's hours: with no time-zone: go by it.

policy.description: #2957, research R11: your layer, as a SignedYourPolicy. Only the keeper sets it (user/setPolicy); a client cannot (user/setSettings refuses this part).

UserSettingsChanged.description: control/userSettingsChanged (#1760): to the person's own clients, when a part or a secret changed, so a pane reads again.

UserSettingsPart.description: user/setSettings (#1760): one part set, or with a null value removed from the user scope.

UserSettingsPartName.description: A part of a person's user settings (#1760, #2410). Each part has one fixed scope: MCP servers, agent configuration, runtimes, cost limits, notices (#2859), outside accounts (#3967) and the time zone (#4818) follow the person. Resources belong to each machine. policy (#2957) is set only by the keeper, through user/setPolicy; user/setSettings refuses it.

UserSuspended.description: user/suspended (#1002, FR-018): to each machine of a suspended person, at hello before its settings and within 5 seconds of a change; off: true ends it.

UserTimeZone.description: The timeZone part of user settings (#4818).

identifier.description: An IANA name, as TimeZone.identifier says it: Europe/London.

YourPolicy.description: Your layer (#2957, data-model.md "YourPolicy"): the rules, kept on the keeper and sent, signed, to your other machines. No agent, MCP tool or workflow can change it (FR-010).

revision.description: One higher at each save. A machine refuses a lower one (FR-011).

person.description: The person's id (the user scope's user, or local for a person with no control plane).

keeper.description: The host id of the keeper (research R4).

YourPolicyState.description: policy/yours (#2957): your layer, which machine is the keeper, and the person key this machine has pinned.

signed.description: The signed copy, when this machine keeps one (#2957): the Mac window passes it to a server over its direct link with policy/applyYours (research R3, path 2).

untrusted.description: Your rules from a copy of your layer this machine cannot trust (#3230): the newest such copy. Its rules do not apply until the person signs them again here.
